synthesis.body: A reviewer subagent reports against the file as it stood when the review was dispatched, not as it stands when the report arrives. During RFC-0092's review, a round-3 finding named an inconsistency between two statements of the same control that an edit landing minutes after dispatch had already removed by giving the control a single home. Applying the reviewer's prescribed fix verbatim would have re-edited text that was already correct, and would have counted a resolved item as an open defect in the handoff. Re-check each finding against current file state before remediating: it separates a live defect from a stale snapshot and costs one grep whenever the finding cites a path and line. This is the discovery-side reason the finding-adjudicator agent exists; where no adjudicator is in the loop, the re-check is the author's job. A related tell is a finding whose origin is the previous round's fix rather than the artifact — that means the review has stopped converging.

title: A reviewer reports against the file as it was at dispatch, not as it is at report time
